title: Catalonia
capsule: The Catalan Republic of 1640–1641 was proclaimed on 17 January 1641 following the Corpus de Sang uprising of June 1640, when Catalan harvesters and miquelets killed the Viceroy of Catalonia, Santa Coloma, in revolt against the billeting of Castilian troops during the Thirty Years' War. The Generalitat under President Pau Claris initially declared a republic under French protection before almost immediately reverting to recognition of Louis XIII as Count of Barcelona on 23 January 1641; French forces and Catalan troops defeated the Castilian army at the Battle of Montjuïc in January 1641. French support proved insufficient over the long term, and Castilian forces retook Barcelona in October 1652; the 1659 Treaty of the Pyrenees permanently ceded Roussillon and Cerdagne (Northern Catalonia) to France.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political events of 1640–1642 are exceptionally well documented in Castilian, Catalan, and French archives; effective territorial control during the conflict fluctuated rapidly and is reconstructed from military campaign records.
